# Niwa Day

> A completely free Windows desktop app that displays your Google Calendar as a floating vertical timeline — today's schedule, quietly in view. A tidy day.

Niwa Day (庭 — Japanese for "garden") is a free, lightweight productivity tool for Windows. It connects to Google Calendar via read-only OAuth 2.0 and renders only today's events as a floating, always-on-top vertical timeline from 00:00 to 23:59. A real-time indicator tracks the current moment, and you can layer personal routines — walks, reading, focus blocks — alongside your calendar events. The window stays semi-transparent and out of the way: no tabs to switch, no window to open.

Key facts:
- Completely free — no cost, no subscription, no in-app purchases
- Download from the Microsoft Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9p0dnstkknp7
- Windows only (desktop application)
- Read-only Google Calendar access — never modifies your calendar
- No analytics or telemetry collected
- Developer: Jimmy Chen (Taiwan) — contact: elminsterii2@gmail.com

## What makes it different

- Shows only today, never a weekly grid — a whole week of events feels like noise; Niwa Day shows just the day you're in.
- A floating vertical timeline on your desktop, always on top but semi-transparent — always near, never in the way.
- A moving time indicator that walks with the day, marking the current moment.
- Personal routines on the same timeline as calendar events — add, drag, and edit your own items.
- Adjustable window size, color, and transparency — tune it once and let it settle in.

## Privacy & data handling

- Authenticates with Google via OAuth 2.0, requesting only the read-only scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly`.
- Calendar data is displayed on your device only — nothing is stored on external servers.
- Access tokens are kept in Windows Credential Manager.
- Follows the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
